name: Handout: Clinical Skills II | Safety Measures in Hospitals
text: Dr. Hanaa Mahmoud Nagdy Ph.D. MBA Hospital Safety 1 Dear students & Transfer Goal Identify hospital environmental hazards and different hospital emergency codes Students’ learning outcomes At the end of this session, the student will be able to .......: Recognize different types of hazard in hospitals. Define different hospital sittings hazards Identify chemical hazards signs list important hospital emergency color codes. Safety program in a hospital is a program that is designed to ensure safe working environments that ensues safety to the employees, the patients and the community. Safety program Any thing that has the potential to cause harm A hazard is any source of potential damage, harm or adverse health effects on something or someone under certain conditions at work. A hazard can cause harm or adverse effects to individuals as health effects Or to organizations as property or equipment losses What is a hazard ? Hospital safety standards: Hospital Hazards Step 4 Step 3 Step 2 Step 1 Types of Hazards Step 5 Biological Hazards PSYCHOLOGICAL HAZARDS ERGONOMIC HAZARDS CHEMICAL HAZARDS Step 6 SAFETY HAZARDS RADIOLOGICAL HAZARDS Add your text here. Subscribe to our channel to watch more creative videos. 9 Accidental spills on workplace floors Tripping hazards like cords and extension cables running across the floor Moving machinery parts that aren’t covered which workers can touch accidentally Electrical hazards like improper wiring, short circuits, overloads. 1. Safety Hazards These are any hazards that you experience while working with people, animals, infectious plants or other microorganisms. Ex: Fungi / mold Bacteria and viruses Harmful plant secretions Blood and other bodily fluid 2.Biological Hazards Bio-hazardous waste is capable of producing an infectious disease in humans and includes at blood, body fluids, discarded sharps, inoculated culture media, tissues and slides. Bottles of blood or body fluids are considered bio-hazardous. High exposure to ultraviolet / sunlight rays. Extreme temperatures both hot and cold (Fire-Explosion-..) Constant loud noise. Radiation – this can be divided into two main types Ionizing Non-ionizing like microwaves, EMF’s, radio waves. 3. Physical Hazards 1. Radiological: B. Fire: Every hospital needs to plan how it will keep its occupants safe in case of fire , smoke and toxic gas leakage. Prevention Detection Suppression Evacuation 20 22 4. CHEMICAL HAZARDS: Liquids ( paints, cleaning products, solvents, acids…) Fumes and vapors from solvents. Flammable materials like explosive chemicals, petrol and diesel Gases like helium, carbon monoxide, propane, acetylene Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) Acetone, acetylene Alcohol, Ethyl (widely used) Methyl alcohol (methanol or wood alcohol; used in laboratories) Benzene (encountered in laboratories) Formaldehyde (used in the laboratory, surgery) Hydrogen Peroxide (used in central processing and central sterile) Lead (used in radiology ) Mercury (used in various kinds of instruments and devices) It relates to mental health and behavioral disorders. Heavy workload/ shifts Lack of social support and community at the workplace Workplace violence Lack of Respect 5 . PSYCOLOGICAL HAZARDS These hazards occur when the nature of the work, work body positions and working conditions cause physical strain (and even mental strain) to your body. These hazards are noted only after it has caused harm to the body. 6. ERGONOMIC HAZARDS Hospital emergency codes are coded messages announced over a public address system of a hospital to alert staff to various on-site emergencies. The codes convey essential information quickly and with minimal misunderstanding to staff while preventing stress and panic among visitors to the hospital. Hospital emergency codes have varied widely by location, even between hospitals in the same community. Codes are posted on placards throughout the hospital or are printed on employee identification badges for ready reference. Codes usually accompanied by a specific location description (e.g., "Code red, second floor, corridor three, room two-twelve"). Use of this code Code Bomb threats black As Bioterrorism is the use of a biological agent (e.g., smallpox, plague, anthrax Evacuation Green Disaster major chemical spill Orange Violent/Behavioral Situation White one of three weather-related situations: snow and/or ice, hurricane, or tornado. Infrastructure Loss or system failure Grey Cardiac Arrest/Medical Emergency –adult Blue Missing Person Yellow Pediatric cardiac arrest Pink Fire Red 34 THANK YOU!

name: PPT: How to Measure Blood Pressure (use this if the above file doesn't work)
text: Measuring and Recording Blood Pressure What is blood pressure? Blood pressure is defined as the lateral pressure exerted by flowing blood on the walls of the arteries 101 Physiology of blood pressure Blood inside artery will put a pressure on the wall Blood flow inside arteries Heart contracts push blood in arteries 101 Physiology of blood pressure Blood will put a maximum pressure which is systole Maximum blood will go into arteries Heart contracts 101 Physiology of blood pressure Blood will put a a least pressure which is diastole blood will go from arteries to veins Heart relaxes Blood Pressure Systolic Diastolic = 120 80 Maximum pressure inside the artery when heart contracts Least pressure inside the artery when heart relax How we measure Blood Pressure Equipements Stethoscope Sphygmomanometer Mercury Sphygmomanometer Are made up of manually inflatable cuffs that are attached to measuring units with mercury-infused tubes. While operating the device, it is important to place the apparatus on a flat surface and in an upright position to get the correct readings. Aneroid Sphygmomanometer Aneroid means “without fluid,” and as the name suggests, this type of BP apparatus doesn’t make use of any mercury and is therefore considered the safest alternative to mercury sphygmomanometers. In the aneroid device, the cuff is attached to a dial gauge with tubing. The gauge head contains mechanical parts that convert the cuff pressure into gauge-based reading. Automatic Digital Sphygmomanometer These devices use an electronic pressure sensor to measure the blood pressure, and the readings are presented on a digital display. There is a difference in the procedure for measuring blood pressure. Why do we use Stethoscope? Stethoscope Try to put your stethoscope on your radial or brachial artery would you hear anything? Korotkoff sounds What we would here Systolic Diastolic = 120 80 Maximum pressure First sound to hear after releasing pressure of cuff Least pressure Last sound to hear while deflating cuff https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UTJvWLi2uCM https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UTJvWLi2uCM So let us measure the blood pressure https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f6HtqolhKqo&t=44s Before the procedure Wash hands Introduce yourself Explain procedure Explain to the patients they might feel discomfort from the cuff but not painful Patient position Setting down on chair if they can after 5 minutes rest Back , leg and arm supported Ask the patients to expose the right arm by rolling up their sleeves Attaching cuff Should be right size Deflated 2cm above antecubital fossa Measuring blood pressure First method is: Palpatory method to get estimated (rough value ) systolic blood pressure Palpate the patient’s radial pulse Inflate the blood pressure cuff until you can no longer feel the patient's radial pulse. Note the reading on the sphygmomanometer at the point at which the radial pulse becomes impalpable ( this point is estimated systolic blood pressure) Deflate the cuff till zero Close the valve Measuring blood pressure Second method is: Auscultatory method to get actual systolic and diastolic reading Place the stethoscope over the brachial artery pulse, ensuring that it does not touch the cuff. Inflate the cuff to 20-30 mmHg more than the estimated systolic blood pressure (obliteration pressure). Then slowly deflate the cuff at around 2-3 mmHg per second The first consistent Korotkov sounds indicate the systolic blood pressure. The muffling and disappearance of the Korotkov sounds indicate the diastolic blood pressure. Record the blood pressure as the systolic reading over the diastolic reading. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UTJvWLi2uCM https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UTJvWLi2uCM To complete procedure Completely deflate the cuff Remove the cuff and blood pressure device Tell the patient readings and explain the significance Record reading in patient file Thank patient Wash your hand https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f6HtqolhKqo&t=44s

name: Watch Me!! Routine Hand wash
text: [Music] hand washing should take you about 1 minute use a timer or count from 1 to 10 in each of the following steps wet hands with water and apply enough soap to cover all surfaces of the hands let the water run smoothly to avoid touching the tap later on rub hands Palm to Palm to obtain a good quantity of foam then rub right Palm over the back of left hand with interlaced fingers and vice versa rub again Palm to Palm with fingers interlaced rub the back of your fingers to opposing Palms with fingers interlocked repeating this action for each hand rub rotationally left thumb clasped in right palm and vice versa to clean the tips of the fingers rub rotationally backwards and forwards with clasp fingers of right hand in left palm and vice versa rinse hands thoroughly with running [Music] water dry hands thoroughly with a single use towel if the tap is not elbow operated use this towel to turn off the tap without touching it directly your hands are now clean and safe

name: Watch Me!! Alcohol Hand Rub
text: please note that this technique is not appropriate when hands are visibly dirty or after using the toilet in these cases hand washing is required hand rubbing should take you 20 to 30 seconds use a timer or count 1 2 3 4 5 in each of the following steps apply a palm full of alcohol-based handrub in a CED hand enough to cover all surfaces of the hands rub hands Palm to Palm then rub right palm over the back of left hand with interlaced fingers and vice versa rub again Palm to Palm with fingers interlaced rub the back of your fingers to opposing Palms with fingers interlocked repeating this action for each hand rub rotationally left thumb clasped in right palm and vice versa to clean the tips of your fingers rub rotationally backwards and forwards with clasp fingers of right hand and left palm and vice versa once dry your hands are now clean and [Music] safe

name: Watch me !!Donning and Doffing N95
text: when wearing a mask for work the following steps can help you correctly put it on and take it off to keep yourself and others safe first wash your hands thoroughly and inspect your mask if it appears damaged do not use it after inspecting the mask up it in your hand with the nose piece at your fingertips and the straps hanging below your hand next lift the mask under your chin with the nose piece up the top strap should go over and rest at the top back of your head if you have a second strap position the bottom strap around your neck and below your ears be sure not to crisscross the straps if your mask has a metal nose clip place your finger tips from both hands at the top of the clip slide your fingertips down the sides of the metal strip to mold the nose area to the shape of your nose now you need to check for a proper seal place both hands over the mask and take a quick breath in to check whether the respirator seals tightly to your face keep both hands completely over the respirator and exhale if you feel leakage there is not a proper seal if air leaks around your nose you need to readjust the nose piece if air leaks at the mask edges readjust the straps along the sides of your head take these steps until you get a proper seal if you do not have a proper seal after repeating the steps ask for help or try a different mask once your mask is on with a proper seal do not touch it before removing the mass first thoroughly wash your hands then reach up and pull the strap over the back of your head without touching the respirator if your mask has two straps remove the bottom strap first followed by the top strap discard the mask in a waste container and again thoroughly wash your hands following these simple steps will help you properly put on and take off your mask and keep you and everyone else safe
